title: Build a Budget
concept: A budget is a plan that helps divide limited money between essential expenses, savings, emergencies, and enjoyable activities.
learningObjective: Learn how to divide a limited amount of money across different priorities so it lasts for the entire month.
primaryMisconception: Budgeting means removing all fun and spending only on essential needs.
secondaryMisconceptions: A budget is useful only when someone has very little money.
Emergency money and savings are unnecessary when all current expenses are covered.
keyTakeaway: A budget is a plan for using money, not a punishment.

screens.title: Thirty Days, One Money Pot
screens.content: You have Rs. 20,000 for 30 days. Can you cover important costs, prepare for surprises, and still leave room for fun?
screens.illustration: A calendar marked 30 Days sits behind a Rs. 20,000 money pot. Six empty envelopes wait beside it.

screens.title: Six Money Jobs
screens.content: The money must cover food, transport, mobile data, savings, entertainment, and unexpected costs for the whole month.
screens.illustration: Six labelled cards surround the Rs. 20,000 money pot.

screens.title: Spend Too Fast?
screens.content: If too much goes to entertainment early, there may not be enough for food, travel, or a surprise expense later.
screens.illustration: Entertainment coins pile up while food and transport envelopes flash low-balance warnings.

screens.title: Fun Can Still Fit
screens.content: A strong plan does not ban fun. It gives important costs, future goals, surprises, and enjoyable activities sensible amounts.
screens.illustration: All six envelopes receive coins, including a smaller but cheerful entertainment envelope.

screens.title: What Makes a Strong Plan?
screens.question: Which approach is most likely to make the money last for 30 days?

options.response: Good thinking. Planning shows whether the full amount can cover every priority.
Fun can belong in a budget, but spending on it first may leave important costs uncovered.
Current costs may be covered, but future goals and surprises would have no money prepared.
A budget is not about avoiding every purchase. It helps money do useful jobs.

screens.title: Build a 30-Day Budget
screens.instruction: Divide Rs. 20,000 across all six categories. Cover the essentials, prepare for later, and avoid spending more than you have.

educationalAssumptions: The Rs. 20,000 must last for 30 days.
Food, transport, and mobile data are required in this situation.
The listed minimums are simplified learning amounts, not real prices for every family.
Savings are for a future goal.
Emergency money is kept available for an unexpected need.
Entertainment is optional, but including affordable fun is allowed.

categories.label: Mobile data
categories.purpose: Required calls, messages, and online access

categories.label: Savings
categories.purpose: Money kept for a future goal

categories.label: Entertainment
categories.purpose: Games, outings, or other enjoyable activities

categories.label: Emergency money
categories.purpose: Money available for an unexpected need

config.remainingBalanceRule: The remaining balance equals Rs. 20,000 minus all six allocations. A completed budget must have a remaining balance of Rs. 0. The learner cannot allocate more than Rs. 20,000.

immediateFeedbackRules.message: Food needs at least Rs. 7,000 in this activity.
Transport is not fully covered yet.
Set aside enough for the required mobile data.
Your current costs are covered, but your future goal needs a place too.
A surprise expense could disrupt this plan. Add some emergency money.
This plan spends more money than is available. Reduce one or more categories.
You included affordable fun while staying within the plan.
This plan can work, but remember that a budget may include affordable fun if you choose.

validCompletionRules: Mobile data receives at least Rs. 1,000.
Emergency money receives at least Rs. 1,000.
Every category stays within its allowed range.

recommendedExampleCompletion.note: This is one balanced example, not the only correct plan.

config.multipleValidBudgetsExplanation: Many budgets can succeed. Learners may move money between categories within the allowed limits. There is no single perfect entertainment amount. A learner may choose more affordable fun or place more money in savings or emergencies.

scoringRules.requirement: Food, transport, and mobile data meet their minimums.
Emergency money receives at least Rs. 1,000.

config.entertainmentScoringNote: Entertainment does not reduce the score when it remains within the allowed budget.
config.correctCompletionState: Any valid 100-point budget is accepted. The recommended example demonstrates that essentials, saving, emergency preparation, and entertainment can all fit in one plan.
config.validationMethod: Check category limits, required minimums, total allocation, remaining balance, and score when the learner submits.

dynamicSuccessMessages.entertainmentIncluded: You also made room for Rs. [entertainment amount] of affordable fun.
dynamicSuccessMessages.entertainmentNotIncluded: Your plan works. You could also include affordable fun by adjusting another flexible category.

config.retryBehavior: Keep valid amounts in place. Highlight only unmet conditions and allow unlimited adjustments.

accessibilityAlternative.method: Provide plus and minus buttons, number inputs, or selectable amounts for every category. Do not require sliders or dragging.
accessibilityAlternative.screenReaderInstruction: Choose an amount for each category. Listen to the remaining balance and status messages, then submit when all Rs. 20,000 has been allocated.

feedback.success: Budget balanced! You covered important costs, prepared for the future and surprises, and stayed within Rs. 20,000.
feedback.incorrect: Your budget needs another look. Check the highlighted category and make sure the full plan stays within Rs. 20,000.
feedback.incomplete: Some money still needs a job. Allocate the full Rs. 20,000 before checking your budget.

screens.title: A Plan With Room to Live
screens.content: You divided limited money between today’s needs, future goals, surprises, and fun. That plan is called a budget. A budget helps you decide where money should go before it disappears. It is useful whether someone has a little money or a lot. Savings prepare for future goals, while emergency money helps with unexpected needs. Entertainment can also belong in a budget when important costs are covered and the total stays affordable.
screens.simpleSummary: A budget gives every part of your money a job.
screens.illustration: A completed budget wheel shows sections for essentials, savings, emergency money, and entertainment, all fitting inside Rs. 20,000.

screens.title: Planning Birthday Money
screens.content: Sara receives Rs. 4,000 for her birthday. She plans Rs. 1,500 for school supplies, Rs. 1,000 for saving, Rs. 500 for emergencies, and Rs. 1,000 for a family outing. Her budget protects important priorities and still includes something enjoyable.
screens.illustration: Sara divides Rs. 4,000 between four labelled envelopes, including a colourful family-outing envelope.

questions.text: Which plan is a complete budget for Rs. 5,000?

options.text: Plan needs, saving, emergency money, and affordable fun
options.feedback: Correct. The plan gives different priorities amounts while staying within the available money.

options.text: Spend until the money runs out
options.feedback: Spending without a plan may leave important costs uncovered before the money period ends.

options.text: Buy fun items and ignore the total
options.feedback: Fun can be included, but the full plan still needs to stay within the available amount.
A budget helps money cover useful priorities. It does not require avoiding all spending.

questions.correctExplanation: A complete budget gives different priorities planned amounts while keeping total spending within Rs. 5,000.
questions.misconceptionTested: A budget is only about restricting spending.

questions.text: Which Rs. 10,000 plan shows that budgeting can include fun?

options.text: Rs. 6,500 needs, Rs. 1,500 saving, Rs. 1,000 emergency, Rs. 1,000 fun
options.feedback: Correct. This plan covers priorities, includes enjoyment, and totals Rs. 10,000.
Entertainment can belong in a budget, but using the full amount would leave other priorities uncovered.
Needs matter, but budgeting can also prepare for future goals, surprises, and affordable enjoyment.
Without planned amounts, it is harder to know whether the money will cover every priority.

questions.correctExplanation: This plan covers important costs, prepares for later, includes enjoyable spending, and stays within Rs. 10,000.

questions.text: Ali has Rs. 6,000. His required costs are Rs. 4,000. Which plan is strongest?

options.text: Cover Rs. 4,000, save Rs. 1,000, keep Rs. 500 for emergencies, and use Rs. 500 for fun
options.feedback: Correct. The plan covers current costs, prepares for later, includes fun, and totals Rs. 6,000.
That may leave too little for the Rs. 4,000 of required costs.

options.text: Use all Rs. 6,000 on current costs
options.feedback: Current costs would be covered, but no money would be prepared for future goals or surprises.

options.text: Ignore emergencies because nothing is wrong today
options.feedback: Emergency money is prepared before something unexpected happens.

questions.correctExplanation: The plan covers current costs, prepares for a future goal and unexpected needs, includes fun, and uses exactly Rs. 6,000.
questions.misconceptionTested: Emergency money and savings are unnecessary when current expenses are covered.

screens.message: You created a plan that covers important costs, prepares for later, and can still include affordable fun.

screens.title: Plan an Imaginary Rs. 2,000
screens.instruction: Divide an imaginary Rs. 2,000 between one need, saving, emergency money, and fun. Check that your four amounts total exactly Rs. 2,000.

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on using a budget to divide limited money between different priorities.
The allocations, remaining balance, example budgets, and scoring rules are mathematically consistent.
The mission uses a guided family-style simulation, mobile data, transport, entertainment, saving, and simple envelopes.
The mission does not discuss investing.
The mission does not discuss investment returns.
The mission does not discuss stocks or markets.
Entertainment is presented as a valid budget category rather than irresponsible spending.
The activity states that its minimum amounts are simplified examples and not real prices for every family.
The mission uses Pakistani rupees and familiar categories such as food, transport, mobile data, savings, and entertainment.
The learner must divide a fixed amount across six priorities without overspending.
The quiz addresses fun spending, emergency preparation, savings, overspending, and the purpose of a budget.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The mission uses three short story screens, one six-category budget builder, and three concise quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The wording is concrete, supportive, and suitable for children aged 8–12.
